nodes.name: CC pretreatment
nodes.procedure: CC was pretreated with HNO3 solution (65%) for 12 h to remove surface impurity, and then rinsed with ultrapure water and absolute ethanol.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, CC was pretreated with HNO3 solution (65%) for 12 h to remove surface impurity, and then rinsed with ultrapure water and absolute ethanol.

nodes.name: Zn-NiFe LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 9 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 3 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 3 mmol Zn(NO3)2·6H2O, 14 mmol NH4F, and 36 mmol Urea were dissolved in 80 ml deionized water. The aqueous solution and pre-cleaned CC were then transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave, which was heated to 120 °C and held there for 6 hours.

nodes.name: Zn-NiFeP phosphatization
nodes.procedure: The CC coated with the precursor of Zn-NiFeP was removed after natural cooling to 25 °C, cleaned with deionized water, and properly dried at 60 °C. The Zn-NiFe LDH/CC precursor was then created by phosphatizing the precursor at 300 °C for 3 hours in an Ar environment. In this phosphatization process, the NaH2PO2 as the phosphorus source was put into the porcelain boat on the upstream side and the CC with the precursor was placed on the downstream side.

nodes.name: d-NiFeP acid etching
nodes.procedure: To create cationic vacancy defects, the above Zn-NiFeP sample was then immersed in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution and acid-etched for 24 hours. Finally, the black color NiFeP nanosheet arrays with cationic vacancy defect on CC substrate was rinsed with distilled water and dried in an oven.

nodes.procedure: For comparison, the pure NiFeP/CC sample was prepared under a similar condition to Zn-NiFeP/CC sample except for 3 mmol Zn(NO3)2·6H2O, which was used during the hydrothermal process.
